explanation.prose: Industrials’ +0.44 cap-weighted divergence is overwhelmingly driven by SPCX, whose +0.81 divergence contributes +0.426—about 96% of the sector reading—while the rest of the basket is much more muted, including CAT at +0.36 (+0.033) and small negative offsets from GE (-0.32, -0.024), RTX (-0.34, -0.019), and BA (-0.49, -0.017). The common thread among the main positive contributors is a shared high-momentum/above-trend setup: SPCX, CAT, GEV, ETN, and PH all post positive divergences and RSI readings in the 55-70 range, but the equal-weight average is only +0.10, showing the breadth is far weaker than the cap-weighted signal.

Energy is a sector-wide euphoric reading: the cap-weighted divergence is +0.33 and the equal-weight average is also +0.32, with all 10/10 constituents sharing the positive sign. The main drivers are the integrated and refining names XOM (+0.108, 33% of the reading), CVX (+0.060), MPC (+0.053), VLO (+0.050), and PSX (+0.034), which are all trading well above their 200-day averages and show positive divergence despite mixed or mostly negative revenue YoY trends. Breadth is aligned rather than contradictory here—equal-weight is nearly identical to cap-weighted—so the euphoric tone is broad, not just a large-cap effect.

Technology’s cap-weighted divergence is +0.12, which is only fair, and the reading is stock_specific because MSFT alone supplies 57% of the sector signal with a +0.071 contribution and +0.39 divergence; AMD (+0.040, +0.81) and AAPL (+0.023, +0.10) are the other main positives. The breadth is a bit stronger than the cap-weighted view, with equal-weight at +0.17 versus +0.12, but the sector still looks driven by a few large names rather than a uniform group, even though 7 of 10 constituents share the sector’s sign.

Consumer Discretionary is a stock-specific divergence story: TSLA’s +0.57 divergence contributes +0.160, which is 134% of the sector reading, while the other big names mostly lean negative—HD at -0.31, MCD at -0.36, BKNG at -0.41, and LOW at -0.34. The equal-weight average is -0.07 versus the cap-weighted +0.12, so breadth is weaker than the headline; 4 of 10 constituents share the sector’s positive sign, and the drivers by absolute contribution are TSLA, HD, and MCD.

Materials reads as stock_specific: Linde alone supplies 88% of the cap-weighted divergence at +0.050, while the sector overall is only slightly positive at +0.06 and the equal-weight average is -0.01. The main positive contributors are LIN (+0.22 div), FCX (+0.25), SCCO (+0.15), ECL (+0.15), and NUE (+0.11), offset by AU (-0.56), NEM (-0.18), and CRH (-0.33), so the breadth is mixed rather than a uniform sector call. The cap-weighted reading is modestly fair even though more names share the sector’s sign than not (6/10), which supports a single-name dominance story more than a broad Materials move.

Consumer Staples is effectively flat on divergence at +0.03 cap-weighted and +0.02 equal-weight, so the breadth picture is similarly neutral even though the signal is stock-specific. COST is the clear driver, contributing +0.027 or 107% of the sector reading with a +0.18 divergence, while WMT (-0.016) and PEP (-0.015) offset it; those names are the main detractors among the large-cap staples, with PEP notably the weakest at -0.24 divergence.

The sector’s near-flat cap-weighted divergence of -0.01 is being driven primarily by META, which contributes +0.067, or 1232% of the reading; the other major offsets are GOOG at -0.035 and NFLX at -0.015. That makes this a stock-specific tape rather than a broad sector story: META is materially positive with div +0.26 and RSI 64, while several large names are negative (GOOG -0.06, NFLX -0.39, APP -1.06), even though 8 of 10 constituents share the sector’s sign. The breadth signal is weaker than the headline on an equal-weight basis, with the equal-weight average at -0.14 versus the cap-weighted -0.01.

Utilities is a stock-specific mix: the sector reads -0.05 on both cap-weighted and equal-weight, but the divergence is driven mainly by Constellation Energy (+0.49 divergence, +0.068 contribution) and Vistra (+0.42, +0.029), both high-RSI names trading above their 200-day averages, against a larger group of defensive utilities with negative divergences such as NextEra (-0.25, -0.053), Duke (-0.18, -0.021), and Southern (-0.17, -0.022). The breadth is not masking a cap-weight/equal-weight split here—the equal-weight average also sits at -0.05—so the story is concentrated in a few names rather than a sector-wide re-pricing.

Financials reads mildly negative at -0.06 on cap weight, but the breadth is a bit weaker at -0.12, so the equal-weight average shows more underlying softness than the headline. The verdict is stock-specific: JPM alone supplies 52% of the sector reading and is the main drag at div -0.17, while BRK-B (+0.11) and V (+0.17) offset it; those positives are coming from payments/financial infrastructure, whereas the negatives cluster in banks and brokers such as BAC (-0.29), GS (-0.38), and MS (-0.31).

Health Care’s cap-weighted divergence is only -0.08, and the reading is stock-specific because LLY supplies 100% of it with a -0.29 divergence and -0.080 contribution. The main offsetting names are ABBV (+0.27, +0.033), MRK (+0.24, +0.022), and TMO (+0.26, +0.017), while JNJ (-0.25, -0.041) and GILD (-0.45, -0.021) pull the other way; these are mostly large-cap pharma/biopharma and health-services leaders rather than a single sub-industry move. Breadth is not as weak as the cap-weighted signal: 6 of 10 constituents share the sector’s negative sign, but the equal-weight average is only -0.03 versus -0.08 cap-weighted, so the heavier weights are doing most of the work.

Real Estate’s cap-weighted divergence is -0.14 and the equal-weight average is also negative at -0.15, so the weakness is broad rather than isolated. The main drags are WELL (-0.039), PLD (-0.035), SPG (-0.023), and O (-0.022); 8 of 10 constituents share the sector’s negative sign, and WELL alone supplies 28% of the reading. The equal-weight figure essentially matches the cap-weighted one, confirming the breadth story, while EQIX (+0.021) and DLR (+0.006) are the only notable positive offsets.

latest.narrative: Industrials is still the most euphoric sector at +0.44, but it remains a stock_specific read: SPCX contributes 96% of the signal, the equal-weight divergence is only +0.10, and the sector is up just +0.02 from the prior snapshot. Energy is the cleanest broad-based positive at +0.33 with a sector_wide verdict, 10/10 constituents sharing the sign, and an equal-weight divergence of +0.32; XOM supplies 33% of the contribution. On the weaker side, Real Estate is the lowest at -0.14 and Utilities is still slightly negative at -0.05, though Utilities improved by +0.09 since the last read. The most notable change since the prior snapshot was Utilities at +0.09.
